relevant_main_commit.title: perf(ui): reduce style matching in common interactions (#194012)

proven_snapshot_differences.toolchain_difference: Node 26 local vs Node24 hosted; Vite8.3.5 both. The specific byte contribution of Node/toolchain differences was not isolated.

decisions: The CSS-only correction demonstrably saves 37 normalized gzip and 450 raw bytes in the available matched same-worktree Node26 normal builds.

Chat boot JS is exactly 1,288,657 bytes both before and after the CSS correction; this correction introduces zero measured chat-JS growth. That does not prove the original entire PR chat-JS effect on current main.
The new local candidate still fails three budgets (118 CSS gzip,187 CSS raw,459 chat JS gzip); neither CSS parity nor build success changes this verdict.

Do not compare the old hosted candidate with the new local build to claim a 1,758-byte repair saving: 1,308 raw bytes of that difference already existed between old local and hosted snapshots. The true matched repair saving is450.

Do not label all remaining overage inherited: no matched current-main/new-merge artifact pair has been measured for this new correction. Existing hosted old base/candidate provides old pre-repair attribution only.

No further unrelated CSS/JS cleanup or budget raise is justified by mixed snapshot results. Root should obtain exact new-head normal hosted performance attribution at its actual main parent, preserve the known local failures in body evidence, and fix only any confirmed contributor regression.
limits: No newly built baseline or refreshed CI was requested by this read-only lane.
The old hosted main was already over CSS gzip and chat JS budgets, but that alone does not excuse contributor growth.
Known UI human scope hold remains independent of technical performance/proof.
